If there's no vehicle, then there's no ray cast and in the beginning of `SceneTree::physics_process`, `flush_transform_notifications` will be called. This sets the correct position on the physics server, thereby avoiding the bug.

Possible fixes:

* In `SceneTree::iteration_prepare` we now conditionally call `flush_transform_notifications` based on if physics interpolation is active. Calling this unconditionally fixes the issue because it means the transforms will be flushed before the vehicle does a ray cast. This fix probably means you can still trigger the same problem if you do a collision query in the `_input` gd script function.
* Changing JoltBody3D to only enqueue call queries when we're not adding objects ourselves. I did this in https://github.com/jrouwe/godot/tree/115322 and that fixes the issue. The downside of this change is that the vehicle ray cast will see the body at (-1 0 0) instead of at (2 0 0). Note that this was the case in 4.5 beta 3 too.
* Ideally, whenever you make a change to a body, the transform will be immediately pushed to the physics server. I don't know why notifications are turned off in the 1st callstack. Changing that would also be a possible fix.

@mihe What do you think is the correct fix here?

Edit: As an alternative to https://github.com/jrouwe/godot/tree/115322 it is maybe safer to only have an activation listener active during `PhysicsSystem::Update` (activating it just before that call and deactivating it right after).

Yikes! That looks like it took a while to distill down to an MRP. I appreciate the effort, from both of you.

> As an alternative to https://github.com/jrouwe/godot/tree/115322 it is maybe safer to only have an activation listener active during `PhysicsSystem::Update` (activating it just before that call and deactivating it right after).

Yes, that would seem like the most appropriate fix here. I doubt I would've caught this bug even if I'd known that the activation listener would be called outside of the simulation step, but my assumption at the time was that it wouldn't be.

I took the liberty of putting up a pull request for it: #115364

> Ideally, whenever you make a change to a body, the transform will be immediately pushed to the physics server. I don't know why notifications are turned off in the 1st callstack.

This is meant to be an optimization. See [`Node3D.force_update_transform`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_node3d.html#class-node3d-method-force-update-transform).
